sector: Maritime/port (solid bulk / iron ore export terminal, Brazil)
hitl_conditions: Not discussed as a change; the user configures routes, demand, capacities and ACS/objective weights through the tool interface, tests schedules virtually before applying them to the real terminal and reads the simulation analysis report to identify improvements.
key_finding: AnyLogic agent-based simulation coupled with an Ant Colony System scheduler, validated against real terminal KPIs (deviations under 5%), cut total ship stay time from 199.6 h to 194.3 h in the base scenario (84.8 h with simultaneous yard-to-ship routes), with estimated demurrage savings of USD 130,750-788,969 within about five minutes.

quotes.text: a Digital Twin (DT)-based tool for optimizing scheduling in solid bulk export port terminals. The approach integrates agent-based simulation with the Ant Colony System (ACS) metaheuristic to efficiently plan railway unloading, stockyard storage, and maritime shipping.

we propose a hybrid optimization approach based on a constructive heuristic followed by refinement using the Ant Colony System (ACS) metaheuristic. The core objective is to minimize the total stay time of ships at the terminal

In the context of ore export terminals, the DT enables testing of scheduling strategies in a virtual environment before they are applied to the real system. This contributes to more informed and robust decision making.
Additionally, the tool generates an analysis report with the main problems encountered during the simulation, allowing the user to identify opportunities for system improvement.
After applying the improvement procedure, a better solution was obtained, reducing the total stay time to 194.3 hours—equivalent to a reduction of approximately 5.2 days in ship queue time.

Furthermore, the implementation and integration of other techniques, such as Greedy Randomized Adaptive Search Procedures (GRASP) and machine learning, are suggested, aiming for more effective strategies for dynamic and complex scenarios.
